title: tk herd cleanup prints "removed" above its own FAILED lines
description:
Operator-caught (2026-08-20): a closed tick still had its worker, worktree, branch and manifest on disk, after cleanup had twice reported it removed.

  tick      is0  removed
    FAILED  remove-workspace wBY
            herdr worktree.remove failed: dirty_worktree_requires_force: ... contains modified or untracked files
    skipped delete-branch    tick/is0 (an earlier step failed)
    skipped remove-manifest  ... (an earlier step failed)
  Error: cleanup did not complete (is0: removal failed)

The exit code is correct (1) and the detail is correct. The SUMMARY LINE is wrong: it says "removed" before knowing whether removal succeeded, directly above the FAILED lines that say it did not. A caller reading the per-tick line — which is the obvious thing to read, and what the orchestrator did — gets the opposite of the truth.

Fix: the per-tick line must reflect the outcome (removed | FAILED | refused), decided after the steps run, not printed as a header before them. Consider whether the same header-before-outcome pattern exists in the other herd commands.

Related orchestrator error worth recording rather than hiding: the run filtered this through `grep -E "^tick"`, which kept the misleading line and discarded the FAILED detail — the same class as the already-recorded rule about never piping a mutating command through head/tail. A correct summary line would have made the filter harmless; both should be fixed.
